headline: Comparative genomics resolves gene family evolution across fungal and protist microbes
label: Microbial Comparative Genomics
summary: Recent genome resources and structure-based phylogenetics expose lineage-specific gene families in fission yeasts, lactic acid bacteria, and marine amoebae.
synthesis: The dominant thread is comparative inference of gene family evolution across microbial lineages. The SOG resource provides orthogroup assignments, alignments, phylogenetic trees, and synteny views across Schizosaccharomyces genomes, enabling systematic tracking of gene conservation within a single genus. In the honeybee symbiont A. kunkeei, predicted structures and phylogenies of very large extracellular proteins in fructophilic lactic acid bacteria indicate recombination-driven evolution of giant surface proteins. A draft genome and transcriptome of marine Entamoeba marina, assembled from Nanopore and Illumina reads, report reduced virulence gene families in the context of attenuated pathogenicity and marine adaptation. What is new is the pairing of structural and phylogenetic resolution of giant surface proteins with genome-scale comparisons in less-studied microbial lineages.
